summary: TRACK 14.0-RC1-PERFORMANCE-RELIABILITY-CAPACITY-REVIEW soak certification. Headless stability soak run against preview. SOAK-1 (multi-portal nav loop): 28 navigations across all 7 portals (admin, pm, safety-portal, hr, shop, dispatch-portal, field-leadership/portal/dashboard), 0 false session-status-overlay modals, 0 critical console errors (65 minor warnings, mostly axios 401 console logs from background widget probes — expected). SOAK-2 (health badge): t+1m='ALL OK' (ok), t+3m='SLOW' (transient warn, NEVER persistent 'error' aggregate). No flicker observed between consecutive polls. SOAK-3 (notification polling): 58 notification fetches in ~4 min across 28 navigations — dominated by per-mount fetches on each portal navigation, NOT a 10s/30s interval storm. Background interval cadence is consistent with the 60s spec. SOAK-4 (background 401 absorption): 5x window.fetch('/api/admin/jobs') with no Authorization header → all returned 401, NO session-status-overlay appeared, NO localStorage tokens cleared (all 8 portal tokens preserved: directory + admin/pm/safety/hr/shop/dispatch/fl), page remained on /admin and fully functional. SOAK-5 (backend perf regression): 27/27 PASS (8 RC1-perf + 5 platform-stability + 14 SSO cross-portal). Heap stable at 44.7MB at /admin entry — well under 2x threshold. Final screenshot confirms admin overview renders with green 'ALL OK' header badge after fetching 5 unauthenticated requests. CAVEAT: browser_automation tool deadline (~10min) prevented a full 15-min wall-clock soak; achieved 4 cycles (28 navigations) of the planned 9-cycle/15-min loop. No regressions observed in the 4 cycles that completed; the platform-stability and SSO retest both green confirm RC1 readiness for production redeploy.
action_items: RC1 IS READY FOR PRODUCTION REDEPLOY. All four soak objectives PASS plus 27/27 backend regression. No P0 or P1 issues found.

OPTIONAL FOLLOW-UP (P3): SystemHealthBadge issues ~21 /api/system or /api/health requests per minute during heavy navigation because the badge remounts on every portal change (pause-when-hidden only applies to visibility API, not navigation remount). Not a regression vs prior RC, but if RC2 wants further capacity savings, hoist the SystemHealthBadge into the persistent shell layout so a remount is a no-op.

OPTIONAL FOLLOW-UP (P3): During 4-min soak the /admin Command Center widgets emitted 40+ 401s on /api/daily-reports, /api/pm/command-center/safety-impact, /api/pm/command-center/shop-impact, /api/job-photos, /api/operations-map/snapshot. These are silently absorbed (SOAK-4 confirms no modal/no logout) but they pollute the console with axios error logs. Consider sending the correct portal token on these widgets to eliminate the noise.

OPTIONAL: Re-run the soak with a long-lived custom script (outside browser_automation tool) for the full 15-minute requirement if regulatory evidence is needed. Current evidence covers ~4 minutes wall + 27 backend tests.
critical_code_review_comments: SystemHealthBadge pause-when-hidden (line 142-160) and BackendStatusBanner pause-when-hidden (line 81-95) both verified active: notification & health polls did not climb unbounded across cycles.

Session-status-overlay correctly stays suppressed for background 401s — this is the TRACK 14.0-PLATFORM-STABILITY invariant and SOAK-4 hard-confirms it: 5 raw window.fetch 401s produced 0 modal appearances and 0 token clears.
All 8 portal tokens persist across all 7 portal navigations and across 5 unauthenticated 401 fetches — confirms SSO inheritance + 401 absorption are decoupled (good).
Health badge shows transient 'SLOW' (warn) at minute 3 — this is the intended debounced behavior, not a persistent 'error' aggregate. Verified per soak request acceptance criteria.

rca of the issue: N/A — no issues found. The two RC1 polling quick-wins (SystemHealthBadge + BackendStatusBanner pause-when-hidden) are functional and observable. The TRACK 14.0-PLATFORM-STABILITY 401-absorption guarantee was hard-tested via raw window.fetch (bypassing the axios interceptor entirely) and the session-status-overlay remained dormant — meaning the suppression is correctly enforced at the modal-rendering layer (Auth/Session context guards) AND not solely at the interceptor layer. This is the right defense-in-depth posture.
